brief: A PLA dome: exactly half of a 70 mm sphere, sitting flat side to the right side, hollow on the inside. It carries no load, so there is no load case.
note: Released with every check passing, and the STL closed across its open side: the cavity was cut by the very plane that cuts the dome, the field was nought across the opening and above it on either side, and the grid's samples lay on that plane. Each was counted as material, and the mesh drew a skin of no thickness there, twice, back to back -- a slicer showed a filled disc. The mesh's own count said so: one piece of 89,778 mm^3 with a sealed void of 75,229 mm^3.

document.name: PLA Hollow Hemisphere Dome
document.description: A hollow dome formed from exactly half of a 70 mm sphere, wall 2 mm thick, open at the flat face which is oriented to the right (+X). Built as a sphere intersected with a half-space box to take the hemisphere, repeated at a smaller diameter for the cavity, and subtracted to leave the shell.

parameters.description: Diameter of the full sphere this dome is half of
Shell wall thickness; not stated in the brief, assumed for buildability
Diameter of the cavity sphere, derived so the wall stays wall_thickness everywhere

features.description: Covers the half of the sphere kept (X from -outer_diameter to 0), its right face passing exactly through the sphere's centre so the flat face lands at X=0, facing +X (right).
The solid outer hemisphere, flat face at X=0.
The solid inner hemisphere defining the cavity, same flat plane at X=0 so the cavity is open at the flat face.
Hollow dome shell, wall_thickness thick, open at its flat (right) face.

requirements.statement: With the flat face oriented to the right (along X), the dome's extent along X equals the hemisphere's radius, 35 mm.
requirements.rationale: A hemisphere's height from its flat face to its apex is the sphere's radius; orientation puts this along X.

requirements.statement: The dome's extent along Y equals the full 70 mm diameter of the flat circular face.
requirements.rationale: The flat face is a 70 mm diameter circle lying in the YZ plane given the stated orientation.

requirements.statement: The dome's extent along Z equals the full 70 mm diameter of the flat circular face.
requirements.rationale: The flat face is a 70 mm diameter circle lying in the YZ plane given the stated orientation.

requirements.statement: The dome is formed from exactly half of a 70 mm diameter sphere.
requirements.rationale: The brief states the dome is half of a 70 mm sphere, so the governing sphere diameter must be declared as a parameter driving the hemisphere geometry.

requirements.statement: The dome's shell shall be 2 mm thick (assumed: the brief gives no wall).
The dome's flat face shall be turned to the right: a rim 2 mm wide, at least 214 mm^2 of it lying flat there.
The flat side shall be open, 33 mm deep at the middle: half of a hollow sphere.

assumptions.statement: The dome is open (uncapped) at its flat circular face, forming a hollow shell with the interior accessible from that face, consistent with typical 'dome' geometry.
assumptions.rationale: The brief calls the part a dome and says it is hollow inside; a dome conventionally is an open shell closed only by its curved surface, not a fully sealed sphere-half.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the flat face were meant to be capped/closed, the part would instead be a sealed hollow hemisphere, changing both its function and its sealed-void count.

assumptions.statement: 'Flat side to the right' is taken to mean the flat circular face's normal points along the +X axis, with the dome's curved surface extending in the -X direction from that face.
assumptions.rationale: The brief gives no explicit coordinate frame; +X as 'right' is the conventional default for a part orientation note.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If 'right' refers to a different axis in the intended assembly/view, the bounding-box axis assignments (X vs Y vs Z) would need to be swapped, though the part's shape is unaffected.

assumptions.statement: The walls are 2 mm thick: the brief says the part is hollow and does not say how thick its walls are.
assumptions.rationale: 2 mm is a usual wall for a small printed or machined part, and some wall is needed to build it.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: The walls are thicker or thinner than wanted; the outside size is unchanged.
